body: Pershing Square's published criteria: simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses; formidable barriers to entry; limited exposure to extrinsic factors; strong balance sheet; minimal capital-markets dependence; high-quality management/governance; attractive valuation vs intrinsic value. Typically 8-12 positions. Add-on: cheap, convex hedges (credit default swaps in Feb 2020, rate-related options in 2022) where the payoff can be 50-100x premium. Lessons from failures: Valeant violated 'simple and predictable' (growth was acquisitions plus drug price hikes; reported 'adjusted' EPS masked it) - ~$4bn loss; Herbalife short and JC Penney turnaround failed on timing and execution. For an individual: concentrated quality buys on temporary bad news, plus a small, explicit tail-hedge budget (e.g., deep-OTM index puts) only if you understand options; avoid serial acquirers whose organic growth is unclear.
title: Ackman: simple, predictable FCF businesses plus asymmetric hedges
